Gilles' cousin, the male who was on the ground outside of the exit, advised he and his family were out celebrating a birthday as well as St. Patrick's Day. He said he heard an altercation taking place in the female bathrooms and tried to break up a fight involving Hispanic female In his attempts to break up the fight, he was grabbed by the hair and pulled down where he got beaten up. He said he doesn't know who beat him up or what exactly happened, he just knew that it was a misunderstanding. He also said he did not want to be the victim of any crimes and did not want anyone arrested for anything. The female who had a seizure and was transported to the hospital eventually identified herself as Letitia. She became argumentative with hospital staff regarding her restraints. Nursing staff then requested an officer to remove her restraints and he did. Letitia was not willing to answer any questions at that time, and the officer left. The day after, an officer spoke on the phone with Kali, she stated she followed her daughter, Leticia, into the bathroom due to her being upset and punching walls. When Kali entered the bathroom, there were several people yelling, and there were approximately three males inside. Kali's niece, who was also in the bathroom, asked another female why she was taking pictures, and they randomly began fighting. At one point, Kalee was pushed by a female taking pictures, so she pushed her back. Later on, when Kali saw her again, she hit her back, which is the incident seen by the officer in the bathroom while on scene. The officer then informed Kali that she would be receiving a disorderly conduct summons for her actions in striking the female in the face and causing her head to forcefully bounce off the paper towel dispenser. He also told her that probable cause could not be established as to who the predominant aggressors were that began the altercation. The disorderly conduct summons was mailed to her address and she is innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law. Now, to me, nightclubs are rarely about fun. They're about frustration that's been soaking in liquor for hours. Problem is, when a fight starts in these places, it rarely stays contained because these fights spread quicker than a bad rumor. And what makes it worse is the way bars breed disorder because you get cheap drinks, you get bad security and a culture that thrives on one-upmanship. That's practically a guaranteed fight by closing time. And when people are drunk and angry, logic is the first casualty. You can explain the law, you can raise your voice. You can even pull people apart, but someone will always think the smartest move is to throw another punch. And most officers know, no matter how much blood is on the floor, someone will insist that we're just, just defending themselves. And that's the irony. People think a night out is about a skate, but it often ends with an ambulance or a jail cell. And officers see it every weekend because the same scenes repeat, crying victims, screaming suspects, and reports that read like a bad movie script. And it's never new, but it's always ugly. So the next time you see body cam footage inside of a club or bar, understand what you're really looking at. Because it's not just a fight, but a symptom of a culture that creates self-control for a spectacle. And when the punches land in front of the police, it proves one thing. This puzzle doesn't need solving. It needs to be shut down piece by piece before someone doesn't get up off the ground.
